chose: Two of the owner's rulings of 2026-11-21, as built. (1) A screen in an essay is never full-bleed, and its caption sits below it, never over the app's own screen. Every whole screen, a snip with no parts named or a clip frame, is drawn by the screen-zoom composition with no stops (wholePicture). It holds the phone in the room above the frame's foot, where the captions draw, on the series' ground, as large as fits there. No size is aimed at: the foot is the caption band the recorder gives (zoomFoot, captionSpace's tallest band), and a silent essay keeps the whole frame. A clip frame is read as a screen of its PNG's own size, scale 1. (2) #3137, option (b): the lowest row of two or more labelled controls in the release APK is its tab bar only when one of its tabs is selected, or it sits at the foot of what the app draws. At the foot means nothing the app can tap lies below it, and it floats at most BAR_FOOT_SHARE (8%) of the screen above the app's lowest edge, since the shell's bar is a pill on a margin of max(0.75rem, the safe-area inset). The width rule (BAR_SPAN) is gone. tabBar is pure, in lib/snips, and tested. Its limit: on a screen with no bar, two labelled buttons that are the lowest thing on it read as one, unless ACTS keeps them out. The bar marks its open tab with aria-current, which the device's tree may not report as selected, so the foot is the signal that finds it. The next Snips Capture run on main is the first real dump it meets.
options: whole screens through screen-zoom with no stops; the bar by its foot or a selected tab
whole screens as plain stills fitted into the frame; the bar by its span
a device-frame composition of its own
gray: The owner decided what is seen (not full-bleed, the caption below the screen) and which signal finds a bar. How each lands in code is a choice: reusing screen-zoom rather than a still or a new composition, and reading 'the bottom edge' as the foot of what the app draws, within a floating bar's margin, with nothing tappable below.
